name: Romamti-Eser
title: Levitical musician in the temple
summary: Romamti-Eser was one of the fourteen sons of Heman, who was one of David's foremost singers and musicians in the temple. He was appointed by lot to lead the twenty-fourth division of temple musicians. His name probably means "I have exalted help" and testifies to his father's praise of God.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as a son of Heman
keyEvents.description: Romamti-Ezer is listed among the fourteen sons of Heman, all of whom were appointed to musical service in the house of the Lord under King David.

keyEvents.title: Appointed for musical service
keyEvents.description: The sons of Heman, including Romamti-Ezer, were set apart to prophesy with harps, lyres, and cymbals in temple worship.

keyEvents.title: The Twenty-Fourth Division
keyEvents.description: By lot, the twenty-fourth lot fell to Romamti-Ezer, who was given responsibility for leading his division of twelve musicians in temple service.

keyEvents.title: Organization of Temple Service under David
keyEvents.description: King David organized the Levites into divisions for singing and music as part of the extensive preparations for the temple that his son Solomon would build.

keyEvents.title: God's promise to Heman through his sons
keyEvents.description: God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters as a blessing, and all the sons served under their father's leadership in God's house with music.
